inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For Tiny Worlds (checked 2026-11-15): VisualCoreMath has OrbitCamera (distance clamped to 0.01...1,000,000, pitch to +/-89 degrees; view, projection, project and ray), OrbitBounds and OrbitViewBounds (pitch limit, distance range, target radius, field-of-view range, clearance sphere; added at A05-P03), CameraRail, Mat4, Vec3, Quat and StableHash; VisualCoreScenes has Mesh, MeshBuilder, MeshShapes, normals, MeshBounds, validation, digest, MeshCache and StreamingBudget (see the geometry row) and the gesture recognizers; VisualCoreSimulation has SeededRandom, SeedDerivation, SceneClock, Tween and Timeline; VisualCoreDiagnostics has QualityGovernor, QualityProfile, TessellationChoice and DeviceConditions; VisualCoreRendering has MeshRenderer (one directional Lambert light plus an ambient fraction, one colour per draw, optional MeshFog), DepthMeshPass, ParticleRenderer, RenderTarget.readPixels, RenderHost.renderOffscreen, StillCapture and ProcessMemory; VisualCoreExperience has ExperienceStorage and the declared quality tiers. Missing in every framework product (grep 2026-11-15): a CPU seeded noise or height-field generator (vc/noise.glsl is GPU-only), instanced mesh drawing (ParticleRenderer draws instanced quads only), per-vertex colour or any material model beyond one colour per draw, ray intersection against boxes, spheres, triangles or height fields, and mesh level-of-detail selection beyond TessellationChoice segment counts.

RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider chooses an RGBA8 ES3 config with no guaranteed depth buffer, so the window surface is colour-only), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler and context generations; pause/resume, replaceScene, recreateContext, renderOffscreen and destroy; scenes implement RenderScene setup/resize/render/teardown. All EGL and GL work runs on the main thread. Tiny Worlds' world (document, seeded terrain and prop generation, placement rules, camera limits) is GPU-free CPU work done at load or edit time, never every frame; finished meshes are uploaded on the main thread and drawing reads the finished world and never changes it. Depth comes from DepthMeshPass's owned off-screen target copied to the framebuffer, never from a changed window configuration. Tiny Worlds adds no EGL or GL context of its own.

ResourceRegistry creates buffers, textures, programs and render targets under a ResourceBudget and rejects stale handles after a generation change; makeRenderTarget(depth: true) adds a 24-bit depth renderbuffer. ShaderProgram, ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary (#include expansion with line maps) compile bundled GLSL; the vc/ library holds color, field, hash, noise, palette and sdf helpers. Pipeline = ShaderProgram + RenderState, applied by GLState.apply (RenderState.opaque3D: depth test and write, back-face culling). MeshRenderer draws one Mesh with Lambert lighting from one light direction plus an ambient fraction in one premultiplied colour, with optional linear eye-depth MeshFog; DepthMeshPass draws a list of items (renderer, model transform, colour) with depth testing into an owned depth target and blits the colour to the framebuffer, on screen and off screen alike. FullScreenShaderScene, ParticleRenderer (instanced quads) and the effects graph (copy, colorMatrix, blur, bloom, distort, composite, feedback, flashLimit; EffectScene, EffectRenderer) are available for skies, atmosphere and grading.

Mesh (positions, normals, uvs, UInt32 indices; plane, cube, uvSphere) and the R02-F05 compiler MeshBuilder under a MeshBudget (default 262,144 vertices and 1,572,864 indices) with welding; shapes surface (a parametric grid of columns x rows with optional closed directions and shared seams), revolution, extrusion, tube and bevelledBox; validate() -> MeshReport (winding, degenerate triangles, boundary edges, closedness, budget); smooth normals with a crease angle and flat normals; MeshBounds (axis-aligned box, centre, enclosing radius, contains); a stable digest; MeshCache bounded by entries and bytes; StreamingBudget levels (behind, ahead, draw distance, element share) with vertex totals and fits(level:perPieceVertices:budget:); TessellationChoice segment counts per quality level. No noise, no height-field generator, no ray intersection and no level-of-detail mesh selection exist.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies the quality level (QualityGovernor over the experience's QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions thermal state and Low Power Mode) and memory/scene-phase events, and renders stills (renderStill); ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls) to Experience; ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers; ExperienceStorage is the per-experience sandbox; ExperienceFeedback routes haptics and announcements; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (eleven registered, A01-A11, checked 2026-11-15; Tiny Worlds joins in A12-P01 and stays unregistered and unavailable in A12-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets). Tiny Worlds version 0.1 needs no microphone, camera, photos, motion or location; saved worlds and their thumbnails live in its own storage, so no usage description or privacy answer changes.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 113 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-15 (shared checks including app-contracts, which checks every docs/apps/*/visualcore-contract.json, package and app builds/tests, experience-release and copy-claims steps of A04-A11, verify steps of A01-A11 on iOS 27 and 26, release audits of the one app, the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check).

Tiny Worlds owns its domain (the world document with preset, seed, terrain parameters, placed props, light settings and schema version; the island, asteroid garden and miniature city packs; the prop catalog and placement rules; the world light; world-specific camera limits and ground clearance; the detail-tier policy with prop, draw and thumbnail caps; saved worlds and thumbnails; the spoken world and camera description; copy and content licenses) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/TinyWorlds/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A12-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: the orbit camera and its bounds (VisualCoreMath), mesh building, shapes, normals, bounds, validation, digests, caches and streaming budgets and the seeded noise and height fields to come (VisualCoreScenes), seeded random numbers (VisualCoreSimulation), mesh drawing, depth and still capture (VisualCoreRendering), quality, persistence and storage (constitution Principle II, A12 section). Infinite Geometry's GeometryCore and Audio Odyssey's WorldPieces stay experience code and are not copied. ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in the A12 regression baseline document (docs/apps/tiny-worlds/regression-baseline.md) with the phase-start commit 9315c27e.

SeededRandom (SplitMix64) and SeedDerivation give reproducible streams from one seed; Mesh.digest, StableHash and StateDigest fingerprint generated geometry and state so the same world document gives the same terrain and composition; MeshCache keeps rebuilt meshes out of the render callback; MeshBudget, StreamingBudget, TessellationChoice, QualityProfile and QualityGovernor bound vertex, index and element counts per quality level. Audio Odyssey (A07) generates seeded landscape pieces with watertight joins and Infinite Geometry (A05) caches compiled meshes this way, both in experience code; Tiny Worlds will use the same framework pieces.

matrix.capability: 3D scenes: several lit procedural meshes drawn per frame with correct occlusion through RenderHost on the main thread, with optional linear depth fog, on screen and off screen alike
matrix.source: brainstorm: 3D scenes; constitution A12 consumer, not fork
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (DepthMeshPassTests: the nearer of two meshes wins in both draw orders on screen and off screen, recreated contexts match; MeshRendererTests; MeshFogTests; RenderHostTests). Each item is one draw call of one renderer; a renderer can be drawn several times with different model transforms. Assembling a world's draw list (terrain, props, water, sky) under a draw budget is the experience's scene code (G-DETAIL caps the count). The audit does not measure performance.

matrix.capability: Camera and navigation: perspective orbit camera (target, distance, yaw, pitch, field of view, clip planes, view and projection), orbit, pinch zoom and pan inside bounds (pitch limit, distance range, target radius, field-of-view range, clearance sphere), with touch recognizers and deterministic arbitration
matrix.source: brainstorm: camera and navigation
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreMathTests (OrbitCameraTests, CameraBoundsTests, OrbitViewBoundsTests) and VisualCoreScenesTests (GestureTests, GestureArbiterTests). The comfort and terrain-clearance part of version 0.1 feature 2 is row M07.

matrix.capability: Procedural meshes: meshes built from code under a vertex and index budget (parametric surface grids, revolution, extrusion, tube, bevelled box, sphere, cube, plane) with welding, smooth or flat normals, bounds, validation and a stable digest
matrix.source: brainstorm: procedural meshes; constitution A12 visuals are code
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests (MeshBuilderTests, MeshShapeTests, MeshNormalsTests, MeshValidationTests, MeshBoundsTests, MeshDigestTests) and VisualCoreRenderingTests/MeshCompilerRuntimeTests. Seeded terrain on top of these pieces is row M08.

matrix.capability: Lighting: a scene light shared by every mesh of a world (direction and ambient level, optionally a warm or cool tint), adjustable at run time, legible without colour alone
matrix.source: brainstorm: lighting
matrix.notes: Since A12-P03 (G-LIGHT closed): the world light (azimuth wrapped, elevation 10…85°, ambient 0.1…0.6) is stored in the world document and applied to every renderer's lightDirection and ambient each frame (WorldLightTests; WorldsRenderTests show a lit face darkening when the light moves).

matrix.capability: Materials and assets: distinguishable surfaces (sand, grass, rock, water, metal, glass-like windows) and a catalog of procedural props without model, texture or image files
matrix.source: brainstorm: materials and assets; constitution A12 visuals are code
matrix.notes: Since A12-P03 (G-PROPS closed): four procedural props (tree, rock, house, lantern) are one mesh each with per-vertex colours from licensed prop palettes, drawn with MeshRenderer(mesh:colors:registry:) through the depth pass (PropCatalogTests, WorldsRenderTests).

matrix.capability: Three small world presets: island, asteroid garden and miniature city, each a bundled world document (seed, terrain parameters, props, light, camera limits) that loads, generates deterministically and resets
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 1: three world presets island, asteroid garden, miniature city
matrix.notes: Since A12-P04 (G-PACKS closed): the island (seed 11), asteroid garden (seed 7) and miniature city (seed 5) packs each bundle a terrain, a prop set placed through the editing rules, a light and camera limits inside the global ones; world.pack opens and resets them, budgets hold (≤ 16 props, ≤ 30,000 vertices, ≤ 18 draws) and committed digests pin them (WorldPackTests, WorldsPackTests); author VisualCore project, MIT.

matrix.capability: Orbit camera with constrained zoom and comfortable control: per-world pitch, distance and pan limits, the eye kept above the terrain and outside props, eased orbit and zoom that Reduce Motion calms, a reset view and a control alternative for every camera gesture
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 2: orbit camera with constrained zoom; manual algorithm decision 4; spec edge case camera penetration
matrix.notes: Since A12-P02 (G-CAMERA closed): CameraPolicy keeps pitch 10°…75°, distance 10…30 m and the eye 0.5 m above the highest of 9 terrain samples around it, raising pitch in 1° steps (CameraPolicyTests sweep of 768 views per preset); drag and pinch are sent as view.orbit and view.zoom with control alternatives, eased in the presenter and direct under Reduce Motion.

matrix.capability: Seeded terrain and mesh generation with stable boundaries: deterministic height and shape noise from a seed, a height-field terrain mesh with edge-consistent (seam-free) normals and bounded resolution, generated at load or edit time and identical for the same seed on every device
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 3: seeded terrain/mesh generation with stable boundaries; manual algorithm decisions 1 and 2; spec edge case seams
matrix.notes: Closed by A12-P01 (G-TERRAIN): GradientNoise2D and FractalNoise2D (bit-identical on every device: +, −, ×, floor only) and HeightField (normals from the field with one ring beyond the grid, so pieces sharing an edge agree bit for bit; bilinear sampler; budgeted mesh), host-tested in GradientNoise2DTests and HeightFieldTests; Tiny Worlds' TerrainGenerator pins nine preset terrains by digest (TerrainFixtureTests).

matrix.capability: Prop placement and scene light adjustment: tap or drag a prop from the catalog onto the terrain (snapped to the ground, kept inside the world and apart from other props), select, move and delete it, and change the light's direction and ambient level, each with a native control alternative
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 4: prop placement and scene light adjustment; user journey 3
matrix.notes: Since A12-P03 (G-PROPS, G-LIGHT closed): props are placed, selected, moved, turned and deleted by replayable actions with bounds, sea-level, spacing and cap rules, resting on the drawn terrain; a tap selects the nearest prop by its picking box (Ray3) or picks the ground; every action has a control (WorldEditingTests, WorldsEditingTests).

matrix.capability: Saved world composition and thumbnails: a versioned world document (preset, seed, terrain parameters, props, light, camera) saved and reopened on the device, each with a small off-screen thumbnail image of bounded size
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 5: saved world composition and thumbnails; spec edge case thumbnails
matrix.notes: Since A12-P03 (G-WORLDDOC closed): the world document (schema 2: preset, seed, props, selection, light, view) saves to four slots through ExperienceStorage's atomic writes with 160×120 PNG thumbnails drawn by the session's still renderer; damaged, newer and oversized files are reported; prop transforms reopen bit-identical (WorldDocumentTests, WorldStoreTests).

matrix.capability: Dynamic detail tier based on the GPU and memory budget: terrain resolution, prop count and draw count lowered per quality level under heat, Low Power Mode and memory pressure, without changing the world document
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 6: dynamic detail tier under GPU/memory budget; constitution A12 bounded
matrix.notes: Segment counts per quality level under a vertex budget (TessellationChoiceTests), streaming levels (StreamingBudgetTests), mesh budgets (MeshBuilderTests), the governor and profiles (QualityGovernorTests, QualityProfileTests) and the process footprint (used by VisualCoreExperienceHostTests/EnduranceTests) exist; no level-of-detail mesh selection or prop and draw caps per tier exist in a framework product. The world's tier table (terrain resolution, prop and draw caps, thumbnail size) and its memory-warning response are G-DETAIL (app-local), A12-P05; Core.qualityTiers must match the presenter's levels. A12-P02 adds three terrain detail levels (TerrainDetail: full, half, quarter resolution; 27 meshes validate with every index in bounds) declared as quality levels level-0…2; the tier policy under memory, heat and Low Power Mode remains (G-DETAIL, A12-P05).

matrix.capability: Depth for 3D drawing: depth test and write into an owned off-screen target with a 24-bit depth renderbuffer, copied to the colour-only window surface and to off-screen exports identically, rebuilt on resize and context loss
matrix.source: cross-cutting: depth; spec edge case depth for 3D drawing
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (DepthMeshPassTests, DepthTargetTests, PipelineTests). The window surface stays colour-only; Tiny Worlds never changes the EGL configuration or adds a renderer for depth.

matrix.capability: Picking geometry separate from the visual meshes: coarse boxes or spheres per prop and the terrain's height field hit by a camera ray, nearest hit first, independent of the detail tier
matrix.source: cross-cutting: picking; manual algorithm decision 3
matrix.notes: Since A12-P02 (G-PICKING closed): Ray3 intersects boxes, spheres and triangles (RayIntersectionTests, analytic within 1e-9); Tiny Worlds resolves a tap on the ground by marching and bisecting over the height field (GroundPickTests within 1 mm), separate from the drawn meshes.

matrix.capability: Seeded determinism: one seed and one world document give the same random streams, meshes and composition on every run, verified by digests, with rebuilt meshes cached outside the render callback
matrix.source: cross-cutting: seeded determinism; constitution A12 deterministic, GPU-free worlds
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (SeededRandomTests, SeedDerivationTests), VisualCoreScenesTests (MeshDigestTests, MeshCacheTests), VisualCoreMathTests/StableHashTests and VisualCoreExperienceTests/StateDigestTests.

matrix.capability: Geometry budget: vertex and index caps refused with a typed error, mesh validation, bounded mesh cache, streaming level totals checked against a mesh budget and GPU resources counted under a resource budget
matrix.source: cross-cutting: geometry budget; constitution A12 bounded; spec edge case unbounded geometry
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests (MeshBuilderTests, MeshShapeTests budget cases, StreamingBudgetTests, MeshCacheTests, MeshValidationTests) and VisualCoreDiagnosticsTests/ResourceLedgerTests. Prop, draw and thumbnail caps per tier are the world's policy (M11, G-DETAIL).

matrix.capability: Persistence: settings and saved worlds as versioned documents in per-experience storage with atomic writes, migration and safe recovery from damaged or newer files
matrix.source: cross-cutting: persistence; constitution A12 offline-first and private
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCorePersistenceTests (DocumentStoreTests, NamedLibraryTests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests (ExperienceStorageTests, SavedStateStoreTests). The world document schema is G-WORLDDOC (M10).

matrix.capability: Quality tiers and low power: quality governor fed by thermal state and Low Power Mode, declared quality tiers that lower mesh density and draw load (never the world document), refreshed by the session
matrix.source: cross-cutting: quality tiers and low power; constitution A12 bounded
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreDiagnosticsTests (QualityGovernorTests, QualityProfileTests), VisualCoreExperienceTests (QualityDeclarationTests) and VisualCoreExperienceHostTests (SessionQualityTests). Core.qualityTiers must match the presenter's levels (declared at P05).

matrix.capability: Accessibility and Reduce Motion: system preferences observed, ambient animation and camera easing calmed, rate-limited announcements describing the world and the camera for VoiceOver, a control alternative for every gesture (orbit, zoom, place, select)
matrix.source: cross-cutting: accessibility and Reduce Motion; constitution A12 accessibility
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (AccessibilityPreferencesTests, AccessibilityPlansTests), VisualCoreUITests (SystemAccessibilityObserverTests, AccessibilityPlayersTests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests (GestureAlternativesTests). The spoken world and camera description is experience wording over AnnouncementPlanner (G-PROPS and G-CAMERA carry its tests).

matrix.capability: Lifecycle and context loss: context loss, resize, background and memory warning rebuild every mesh and target from versioned CPU world state; backgrounding pauses ambient animation and never fast-forwards it
matrix.source: cross-cutting: lifecycle and context loss; constitution A12 resilient GPU state
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (RenderHostTests, ResourceRegistryTests, DepthMeshPassTests recreated context, MeshRendererTests recreation), VisualCoreExperienceHostTests (SessionPhaseMemoryTests, ShellLifecycleTests) and VisualCoreSimulationTests/PlaybackStateTests.

matrix.capability: Ambient animation: gentle deterministic scenery motion (water, clouds, drifting asteroids) driven by a scene clock with pause, rate and easing, calmed by Reduce Motion
matrix.source: cross-cutting: ambient animation; user journey 1 (animated scenery)
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (SceneClockTests, TimelineTests) and VisualCoreMathTests/EasingTests. Animation moves drawn transforms only and never changes the world document.

matrix.capability: Licenses and provenance: every preset, prop, palette and shader bundled later records its author and license; only original content
matrix.source: cross-cutting: licenses; constitution A12 licenses; spec FR-A12-006
matrix.notes: Closed by A12-P01 (G-CONTENTLICENSES): every bundled preset and palette records author and license (MIT, original); ContentCatalog refuses missing-license, unsupported-license, out-of-range, invalid-number and duplicate-id; LicenseAudit generates docs/apps/tiny-worlds/content-licenses.md, checked against the catalog by a test. Props and shaders added later join the same audit (G-PROPS, G-PACKS).

gaps.justification: Found in A12-P00: no CPU seeded noise and no height-field generator exist in any framework product; Audio Odyssey's seeded landscape pieces are experience code. Deterministic value or gradient noise with fractal sums from a seed, and a height-field terrain mesh over a bounded grid with a height sampler and normals computed from the field (so adjacent tiles agree on shared edges), are generic and belong to VisualCoreScenes (constitution A12 reuse first, clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests (swift test, no GPU): the same seed gives bitwise identical noise and meshes (digest fixtures), different seeds differ; noise stays within its stated range; two adjacent tiles share identical edge positions and normals (seam-free); the height sampler matches the mesh vertices and interpolates between them; resolution above the MeshBudget is refused with MeshError.budget; NaN/Inf parameters rejected; API baseline additive and the reference regression passes at the X gate

gaps.justification: Found in A12-P00: a draw has exactly one colour and no per-vertex colour or material model exists in any framework product. An optional per-vertex colour stream drawn by MeshRenderer and DepthMeshPass (Lambert lighting and fog unchanged, existing meshes and digests unchanged when absent) lets a terrain be coloured by height or slope in one draw and is generic, so it belongs to VisualCore where generic (clarification 5, A12-P02); named surface palettes stay in the experience.
gaps.test: Host and simulator tests: a mesh with vertex colours renders each region in its colour under the same light within a pixel tolerance; a mesh without colours renders exactly as before (MeshRendererTests and DepthMeshPassTests unchanged); colour streams of the wrong length are refused; context recreation rebuilds the stream; API baseline additive and the reference regression passes at the X gate

gaps.justification: Found in A12-P00: OrbitCamera.ray exists but no ray-box, ray-sphere or ray-triangle intersection exists in any framework product. Ray intersection against simple picking shapes (nearest hit distance and normal) is generic geometry and belongs to VisualCoreMath (clarification 5, A12-P02); which shapes stand for which prop and the ground hit over G-TERRAIN's height sampler stay in the experience.
gaps.test: Host tests: rays hit boxes, spheres and triangles at the analytic distance and normal, including grazing, inside-start and parallel cases; misses return nil; the nearest of several hits wins; a ray through OrbitCamera.ray at the screen centre hits the target's box; NaN/Inf rays rejected; API baseline additive and the reference regression passes at the X gate

gaps.justification: Constrained orbit and zoom already exist in VisualCoreMath (OrbitBounds, OrbitViewBounds with pitch limit, distance range, pan radius, field-of-view range and clearance sphere, tested). What remains is the world's camera policy: per-world limits, keeping the eye above its own terrain and props through G-TERRAIN's height sampler, eased motion with a Reduce Motion variant, a reset view and control alternatives (clarification 5 allows app-local where not generic).
gaps.test: Host tests: every orbit, zoom and pan step returns a camera inside the world's bounds; the eye stays at least the stated margin above the terrain at every yaw and pitch of a sampled sweep; extreme pinches saturate at the limits; the reset view restores the preset camera; eased motion is replaced by direct moves under Reduce Motion; every camera gesture has a control alternative (GestureAlternatives.missing is empty); the spoken camera description is rate-limited

gaps.justification: The prop catalog (procedural shapes from MeshShapes with named palette colours), placement rules (snap to ground, inside the world, minimum spacing, prop cap), selection, move and delete as replayable editor commands, and the spoken world description are the experience's content and editor over VisualCore's meshes, recognizers and G-PICKING (clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests: each catalog prop builds a valid mesh within its budget; a placed prop rests on the terrain height at its position within a tolerance, stays inside the world and keeps the minimum spacing; placement beyond the prop cap is refused with a message; select, move and delete change only the document and replay to the same digest; every action has a control alternative

gaps.justification: The world light (direction from azimuth and elevation within stated ranges, ambient level, optional tint through the draw colour) is a world setting applied to every renderer's existing lightDirection and ambient; no new shading model is needed for version 0.1 (clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests: azimuth and elevation map to the stated unit direction and are clamped to their ranges; ambient is clamped to 0...1; the light is stored in and restored from the world document; non-finite values rejected; a simulator test shows a lit face brighter than a shaded one after the light moves

gaps.justification: The world document (preset, seed, terrain parameters, props, light, camera, schema version), saved worlds and their bounded thumbnails are the experience's data stored in ExperienceStorage through VisualCorePersistence, with thumbnails drawn off screen by the session's still renderer and encoded as PNG (clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests: world documents round-trip and regenerate the same digest; damaged, truncated or newer files are reported and never crash; a write interrupted mid-way keeps the previous file; documents beyond the prop or size caps are refused; a simulator test renders a thumbnail at the capped size, stores it beside the document and reopens both

gaps.justification: The island, asteroid garden and miniature city packs (terrain parameters, prop sets, palettes, light and camera limits) are the experience's bundled content built on G-TERRAIN, G-PROPS and G-LIGHT (clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests: each pack loads, generates deterministically (digest fixture), stays within its vertex, prop and draw budgets, keeps the camera limits valid for its terrain and resets to its document; each records author and license

gaps.justification: The world's tier table (terrain resolution through TessellationChoice, prop and draw caps, thumbnail size) and its response to memory warnings, heat and Low Power Mode are the experience's policy over StreamingBudget, MeshBudget, QualityProfile and QualityGovernor (clarification 5); level-of-detail mesh selection beyond segment counts is not needed for a bounded diorama.
gaps.test: Host tests: each tier's terrain, prop and draw counts stay within the arithmetic bound of its budget; lower tiers never raise a count; changing the tier never changes the world document or its digest; a memory warning drops to the lowest tier and rebuilds within budget; Core.qualityTiers matches the presenter's levels

gaps.justification: Per-content author and license fields for presets, props, palettes and shaders belong to the experience's content definitions (as Physics Playground's and Digital Aquarium's LicenseAudit); the audit starts with the first bundled content in A12-P01 and covers the packs added in A12-P04.
gaps.test: Host tests: every bundled preset, prop, palette and shader records an author and a license and the audit fails on a missing one

11 of 21 rows are available with tests: 3D scenes, camera and navigation, procedural meshes, depth, seeded determinism, geometry budget, persistence, quality tiers and low power, accessibility and Reduce Motion, lifecycle, ambient animation; constrained orbit and zoom (OrbitBounds, OrbitViewBounds) already exist, correcting the clarification's assumption that they were missing.

All gaps are additive and owned: G-TERRAIN (seeded noise and height-field terrain with seam-free normals, VisualCoreScenes upstream) and G-CONTENTLICENSES (app-local) in A12-P01; G-MATERIALS (per-vertex colour, VisualCoreRendering upstream), G-PICKING (ray against box, sphere and triangle, VisualCoreMath upstream) and app-local G-CAMERA in A12-P02; app-local G-PROPS, G-LIGHT and G-WORLDDOC in A12-P03; G-PACKS in A12-P04; G-DETAIL in A12-P05.

No permission and no privacy answer changes; Tiny Worlds stays unregistered until A12-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/TinyWorlds with its targets and first real rules, so the experience package check and the one app are unchanged.
